text:
The Holiday Perfume Sampler Vault is worth every penny! My little review.

I’ve had this set for over a week and have had the chance to test them out and I wanted to share my thoughts.

I’ll start by saying that I bought this set with the intention of potentially exchanging my voucher for La Bomba, Power of You, Vanilla 28, Rare, or Cloud. And I collect minis so I saw value from these minis as is, even without the voucher. With that being said, I already own Paradox and Flora Gorgeous Orchid but the intense versions of both so I’m not interested in these even though, yes they are different. I also own a travel size of Burberry Her Elixir already and a full size of the Burberry Her Intense, so I’m set on this fragrance.

From here, I’ve ruled out Cloud, Wood Sage & Sea Salt, Daisy and La Bomba. I’ll explain why!

Cloud - I like this scent but I don’t at the same time. It’s lovely but I think I don’t like the coconut cream in this. I’m happy with the amount I got off this sample to keep playing with it but I don’t see myself owning a full size.

Wood Sage & Sea Salt - this one I expected not to like since I don’t like citrus/woody scents.

Daisy - while I like the smell of this, it doesn’t last long on me. None of the Marc Jacobs EDT do, so I expected this.

La Bomba - I liked this at first but after wearing it all day, it was a little too synthetic and artificial for me. It did last all day though! Plus, with the amount I got here, I feel like I’m set on it for now.

So that leaves me with Power of You, Rare, Vanilla 28, and Lost Cherry. I have to say I was pleasantly surprised with Tom Ford Lost Cherry. I thought I wouldn’t like it at all but it’s not bad off first impression. It’s very nutty and unique from what I own. I still have to wear it for a full day wear test. I really liked Vanilla 28. This is such a lovely vanilla and surprisingly unique even though I own several other vanilla perfumes. Rare is really good I just wish I got a bit more pistachio from it. It is slightly similar to Burberry Goddess, which I own, and for that, I’m on the fence of redeeming it for this one. Power of You, I still want to test this one out more but off first wear, it’s really fruity and lovely.

I know the exact quantities are listed in the description but decanting some of these really put in perspective the steal this set is for $98. For example, I decanted only half of the La Bomba mini (which is a 0.37fl oz mini) and it filled half of the travel pen. A 0.34fl oz travel size of this retails for $36. That’s a third of the price of this entire set!

This has overall been really fun and I’m excited for when I actually go redeem my voucher! I’m also hoping it comes back in stock so that more people can get their hands on it!

text:
Sephora Sale Recs: Products I use as a soft summer

Products I use regularly and love as a soft summer with light neutral leaning cool skin, level 7 ash light brown hair and grey eyes. I have dry sensitive skin and am sensitive to strong fragrance.

- Natasha Denona “I need a nude palette”. Perfect for neutral leaning cool people. If you are a cool summer, I would look at “I need a cool” instead. Formula is long lasting and easy to use

- Original Benetint. I have been using this product regularly for over 20 years. I have gone through countless bottles. I know dupes exist and I have them. I still prefer the original. I wear this everyday to “underpaint” my existing makeup

- Kosas powder blush in euphoria is my ride or die!! Love the shade, the formula, and the subtle sheen. I have extremely dry skin and this powder formula works for me. I’m planning on buying a backup to put in my travel makeup bag as I fly frequently for work

- Charlotte Tilbury pillow talk fair lip liner is a perfect purple-y pink shade. I have panned this and will repurchase. I also love Morphe lip liner in girl talk for $7 and think it is a great affordable dupe.

- saie liquid blush in chilly. She is pigmented but gives a beautiful dewy finish to the skin! A little goes a long way. This is a great “red” blush if you lean cool

- Clinique pop gloss in sugar plum is my favorite!! No weird scent, just a perfect sheer cool pink. Gone through a full tube already and need to restock

- Merit lipliner in coupe. The wear time is not great but the color is soooo amazing!! I almost think of this more as a lipstick enhancer than I would think of it as a traditional lip liner. The t is more like a lip blur pencil. Love it in a combo with clinging que sugar plum pop

- Merit satin lipstick in millenial pink. The only lipstick I have finished multiple tubes of!! I have been wearing it since it came out. This is my perfect “nude” lipstick as someone who leans cool.

- the rare beauty brow gel in rich taupe definitely gives my brows a snatched look while adding a little bit of color. I love the pencil too.

- the Anastasia Beverly Hills palette in Haze is a soft summer dream!! EVERY single shade is wearable for me. I love using the navy shade as a liner paired with navy mascara. I love the small size. Easily fits in my purse and is my dedicated travel eyeshadow, especially for work trips.

- Westman atelier in dou dou. Despite being described as a “warm” rose, I actually find it is quite cool. Swatches very similar to the saie chilly. Has more of a matte texture if you don’t like a dewy look. I have panned this 2x.

- merit archival blush balm in archival is a perfect muted mauve and acts as a “brown” blush on me. Gives a dewy finish

- makeup by Mario skin enhancer in light medium. This is such a wearable bronzer shade for me! It is not pigmented and very build able. As it is a bronzer, it is warm but it doesn’t pull orange on me.

- tower 28 tinted sunscreen in La cienega. Doesn’t pull orange on me. Super hydrating. I have sensitive skin and I use tretinoin. I layer it on top of chemical SPF 50 for a second layer of protection. I hate foundation but this one works. I prefer it over the ciele one significantly!!

- the ilia lip balm in lullaby rose is a perfect no makeup makeup tinted chapstick. Super hydrating and looks great layered with benetint

- merit blush balm in Stockholm. Less pigment than the archival shade and I like that I can apply it without a mirror. Gives a dewy plump sheen and layers great over benetint. Not long lasting though but looks amazing!

- the merit complexion stick in dune is a perfect neutral to cool shade that doesn’t pull too pink on me and has a bit of grey in it. I love using this a spot concealer and find it blends out beautifully. Have panned multiple times and repurchased over and over.

Products I would skip:

Patrick ta blush in out of office was too pigmented for me.

Rhode in piggy lasted like 2 seconds and didn’t give me as much of a dewy glow as the merit.

Rhode lip gloss in pretzel tasted like kid makeup to me and I personally could not tolerate the scent. It gave me a migraine. Beautiful shade though if you don’t mind artificial flavor/scent.

Unpopular Opinion: 50% Off $40 isn't a deal... It's the REAL price! 😱😱

Has anyone else started feeling burnt out by "sale prices"?

I love luxury and prestige makeup as much as the next person, but lately, I’ve been reflecting on how easy it is to get caught up in high "retail values."

For example: when a lip balm has a regular price of $24 and goes on sale (20% off) we feel like we’re getting an incredible deal. But in reality, $19 and even $15 for a lip balm is still steep, and $15 feels like what the base price should have been in the first place!

It feels like the beauty industry inflates base prices so that sales seem like a steal. This feels especially true for basic items like lip balms, mascaras, and powders.

With the holiday sales coming up, I'm trying to ask myself: Is this actually worth the price tag to me, or am I just getting hypnotized by the "50% off" tag?
Is anyone else changing how they view sales this year?

UPDATE: My last dollars spent here- EVER

I made a post last night about my package missing 7 of my 8 items I ordered. This was a $321.84 order I placed during the friends and family sale. I was told by two associates, one on chat, one on the phone and then a phone supervisor as well, that there was nothing they could do because the weight of the package showed as if all the products were in there (so this was obviously an inside job in a warehouse- IMO).

Anyway, I read through so many of your guys helpful comments, recommending chargebacks with my card, filing a complaint with BBB, messaging LinkedIn higher ups and Sephoras social media profiles, and continuing to call. I am very happy to say that a resolution has been made with this order. So in case anyone else has had this issue with no resolution yet, here is what I did. I filed a complaint with the BBB, and I listed the San Francisco location (I googled where their main office is and that location is what came up). I wrote in as much detail as possible what happened, I included photos of my package and the one item in it, I included the chat messages with Sephora where they said there is nothing they could do, and I included screenshots of the original order from the Sephora app showing what I was supposed to receive, the total spent, and the order number.

I filed this complaint at 11:55pm last night, got a confirmation email from the BBB this morning at 10:54am saying they had accepted this case and forwarded along to Sephora. Then today at 2:04pm I got an email from Sephora Client Relations saying they have seen the complaint with the BBB and have issued me a refund for $277.33 (the total minus the body lotion +tax for that item).

I still stand firm in my decision to not spend another penny at this store. The way I was treated was horrendous as someone who has been a loyal rouge member for many, many years and having to go through these lengths should not be necessary. So be warned, if you insist on shopping this store, do it in person. For me, I’ll stick with ordering directly from the brand’s websites. They have better deals anyway. text:
Why I will never shop at Sephora again (a rant and a warning to others)

This is a long rant/warning about a horrible experience shopping with Sephora online.

Just some background, I don’t really shop at Sephora much, I have maybe bought about three things there, my last purchase being years ago and never online so I don’t have an extensive history with them, positive or negative.

I made a $500 purchase online over a week ago, this was a gift for someone and it was suppose to arrive in two days, unfortunately the courier was OnTrac.

The item reaches the facility (that is only a few miles from where I live) in a day and then stops, days go by and each day the expected delivery date changes to whatever the current day is, but each day nothing shows up, this went on for 7 days. 5 days in I contact Sephora via chat, they tell me if it doesn't show up that day reach out again, so I reach out the following day. I am then told by that chat agent that I should reach out to OnTrac (I am not sure why it is my responsibility to contact THEIR courier, but I do).

I am very patient hoping its just a delay, I reach out to OnTrac a few times (you can only speak to them via chat, they don't have a call line anymore), first I am told they are just backlogged, but later I am told to contact Sephora, then I am told they are "opening an investigation".

The night of day 6 I start reading horror stories online about OnTrac marking things delivered when they lose packages and start freaking myself out, but I figure “there must be more to theses stories, there is no way they marking things they lost delivered to shift responsibility off of themselves and onto the consumers.”

The next morning I contact Sephora again and am told they are escalating my case and I should get an email in 48 hours. I contact OnTrac again, get told once again they will "open an investigation".

Well it happened, later that day I am sitting on the steps at the entrance of my apartment building only an hour or so after contacting OnTrac that last time and I get a notification "my package was delivered", odd because It didn't even change from reached facility to "out for delivery", just straight to "delivered””. I was also sitting right outside my building for the past hour or so reading emails and no one stopped by my building or any of the buildings on my small residential city block.

They actually just marked my $500 order that I am sure they lost "delivered" so it wouldn't be their responsibility anymore, so yes, OnTrac will actually do that.

I contacted OnTrac immediately and asked for a photo of proof of delivery, of course they don't have one, I ask them a bunch of other questions but all they will tell me they will "open an investigation"... (All their responses always sound exactly the same no matter who you talk to, they are obviously just copy and pasted from a sheet)

I then contact Sephora immediately after, both via chat and phone call, they tell me my case was elevated but I will have to still wait at least 48 hours (business days) to find out if they are willing to resend or refund. Two hours later a receive an email basically saying they will not be refunding or resending my item because it was “marked as delivered”, I received this while I was out trying to enjoy my Friday after work.

I go straight home and call Sephora again, the woman on the line tells me the decision is final and I won’t be getting any refund, I ask her for proof of delivery, she says she doesn’t need to show me that. I tell her my whole story and ask how that doesn’t seem suspicious and she tells me they trust what the courier says so its final. I ask more questions and she basically admits that since my item was expensive they aren’t refunding me, so if I had ordered something cheap I would have had a better chance of not getting screwed I guess?

I am simultaneously speaking with agents on chat and I get elevated to a supervisor, everyone I speak with refuses to answer any of my questions as the suspicious nature of the delivery, the fact that OnTrac has thousands of complaints just like mine levied against them. They basically talk down to me and act as if I am lying even thought my delivery was in limbo for over a week and I had been reading out to them for days. How could I have planned all that?

Well after the speaking to the first (truly awful) woman who by the way told me with a straight face she “has never experienced any calls or complaints about OnTrac”…

I decided to call again because I don’t plan to give up easy, I’m not swallowing a $500 loss. By a stroke of pure luck I happen to get a lovely woman, I tell my whole story again just as I had done to all the other agents, once I finish she says “well I see several days ago someone attempted a resend but it was too early, let me try doing one now and see if it goes through”. After a few minutes she informs me it worked and they are resending it, she also added some samples as well for the trouble, she was truly lovely. I thanked her profusely and even stayed on the call so I could give her a 10/10 survey report. (By the way all the other agents and managers I spoke to told me a resend or refund was Impossible and the system would not allow it, liars.)

The item did get resent and arrived within a day or so, I took it straight to the closest Sephora and promptly returned it, I am NOT giving that company a cent.

Never again will I shop with them, this was a wakeup call for me and showed me the truly dire state of online shopping.

Sorry for the long rant, this is really just a warning, if your item gets lost you could be on the hook for it, if any of the low rate couriers Sephora uses decide to falsely mark your package as delivered, or even mis deliver to the wrong building or house (they don’t require photos anymore like they did in the past) you may just be out of luck. God forbid it is an expensive order, that will work AGAINST you and just make Sephora LESS likely to make things right.
